text: BANK OF AMERICA SURVEY SHOWS BIGGEST TECH STOCK SELLING SINCE 2006 Investors slashed technology exposure at the fastest monthly pace since June 2006, according to BofA's fund manager survey. The survey covered 169 investors managing $461 billion, signaling a sharp shift in sentiment toward AI-related equities.

text: 🇪🇺 EUROPEAN STOCK OPTIMISM HITS HIGHEST LEVEL SINCE FEBRUARY, BOFA SURVEY SHOWS Bank of America reports that a net 67% of fund managers expect European equities to rise over the next 1–3 months, up from 44% in October. Investors forecast 5.92% gains over the next 12 months, with 50% citing earnings upgrades as the key catalyst. Switzerland (+30%) and Germany (+27%) are the most favored markets, while France (-60%) hits a record low. Industrials lead sector positioning, while autos (-47%) remain the most underweight.

text: AI BUBBLE TOPS GLOBAL MARKET RISKS, BANK OF AMERICA SURVEY FINDS Bank of America's November fund manager survey shows investors increasingly concerned about risks tied to the AI investment boom. 🔸 34% identify an AI bubble as the biggest tail risk to markets. 🔸 31% cite an AI-related credit crisis as the second-biggest threat. The findings highlight growing concerns over AI valuations, heavy capital spending and debt exposure. Investors increasingly see AI-related shocks as the most significant potential threats to global financial markets.

text: TRUMP DOWNPLAYS MAJOR U.S. SYSTEM OUTAGES, SAYS AMERICANS ARE SAFE President Donald Trump dismissed concerns over recent disruptions affecting Microsoft ($MSFT), JPMorgan Chase ($JPM) and U.S. aviation systems. The incidents included a global Microsoft outage, an FAA equipment failure that grounded flights for more than four hours, and banking transaction delays. Speaking in Manila, Trump said the disruptions were under control and assured Americans that travel remains safe ahead of Thanksgiving. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy estimated the aviation disruption cost the economy billions of dollars.

text: $ANT - AI MODELS IDENTIFY CIVILIANS AND SCHOOLS AS MILITARY TARGETS IN SIMULATED TESTS An independent investigation by Vals, reported by Bloomberg, tested AI models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI, in simulated military targeting scenarios. Researchers found models sometimes identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers and schools as military targets. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 selected a school in Minab, Iran, in 22 of 32 tests, rising to 23 when told the scenario was a game. OpenAI models avoided selecting the school initially but identified it 9–13 times under game framing. Anthropic acknowledged these scenarios violate its policies. The study raises serious concerns about AI-powered military targeting, although the simulations did not assess actual military operations or human oversight.

text: $LHX $HPE - FAA HALTS ROUTER INSTALLATIONS AFTER NATIONWIDE FLIGHT GROUND STOP The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended new router installations following a communications failure that disrupted U.S. air traffic, according to The Wall Street Journal. The incident caused nearly 20,000 flight cancellations and thousands of delays. Investigators suspect a newly installed HPE Juniper router in Arkansas overwhelmed the communications network, affecting radio and radar systems. L3Harris, the FAA's network contractor, is conducting diagnostics with HPE and Cisco. The precise cause remains under investigation.

text: NSA CLASSIFIED NETWORK OUTAGE LINKED TO SOFTWARE UPDATE, NOT CYBERATTACK The National Security Agency's classified communications network, NSANet, is temporarily offline due to a software update, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal. Officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack, easing concerns following recent disruptions involving Microsoft 365, U.S. air traffic systems and JPMorgan Chase. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated that the U.S. is not under cyberattack. The clarification suggests the NSA outage is routine maintenance rather than a national security breach.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: $NVDA - NVIDIA STOPS DISCLOSING SINGAPORE SALES AS REVENUE SURGES TO $104 BILLION Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore-linked revenue after changing its geographic reporting methodology from customer billing addresses to headquarters locations, according to the Financial Times. Its Singapore subsidiary booked $104 billion in external revenue in 2025, up 72%, representing nearly half of Nvidia's global sales. The disclosure change comes amid U.S. investigations into Megaspeed, a major Singapore-based customer suspected of diverting advanced chips to China. Nvidia says most Singapore-billed products were shipped elsewhere. The shift raises transparency and export-control concerns, though it does not establish wrongdoing.

text: $NVDA $HSII $ARM - NVIDIA HIRES HEIDRICK & STRUGGLES TO FIND NEW CEO Nvidia has hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead its CEO search following Jensen Huang's resignation, according to The Wall Street Journal. The search, led by Jeff Sanders, will consider internal and external candidates, with Arm CEO Rene Haas reportedly among those approached. Colette Kress remains interim CEO. Despite Huang's willingness to return, Nvidia's board is reportedly not considering reinstatement. Separately, Wachtell Lipton has been hired to investigate whether Huang disclosed corporate or national security secrets.

text: JPMORGAN WARNS LEVERAGED-LOAN DEFAULTS COULD MORE THAN DOUBLE IN 2027 JPMorgan forecasts U.S. leveraged-loan defaults will surge to 4.5% in 2027 and 4.75% in 2028, up from 1.96% in October. Companies facing AI disruption, elevated borrowing costs and looming debt maturities are particularly vulnerable, especially in software and technology. Of the $862 billion in debt maturing between 2027 and 2029, 46% carries a B3-or-lower credit rating. Meanwhile, high-yield bond defaults are projected to rise more modestly to 2.75% in 2027. The outlook signals mounting stress in corporate credit markets.

text: ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS “WE AIDED, ARMED, AND ABETTED A GENOCIDE. text: $BABA $ABNB $DASH - TRUMP ADMINISTRATION WEIGHS DISCLOSURE RULES FOR CHINESE AI USE The Trump administration is considering requiring U.S. companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, Reuters reports. The proposal, discussed by the Treasury Department and White House, could affect companies such as Airbnb, which uses Alibaba's Qwen for customer service. Rather than imposing outright restrictions, officials are exploring transparency requirements to discourage reliance on Chinese technology. No formal rule has been announced. The move reflects growing Washington scrutiny of DeepSeek, Qwen and Kimi as Chinese AI adoption expands.

text: U.S. MORTGAGE RATES SURGE TO 7.35% AS LOAN DEMAND FALLS The average U.S. 30-year mortgage rate climbed 14 basis points to 7.35% in the week ended November 13, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. Total mortgage applications fell 2.3%, while purchase applications declined 2.5% and refinancing demand dropped 1.5%. The overall mortgage market index slipped to 199.8, reflecting weakening borrower demand. Persistently elevated mortgage rates are increasing affordability pressures and threatening to further slow U.S. housing market activity.

text: ECB WEIGHS DOUBLING BANK RESERVE REQUIREMENTS TO 2%, SAVING €4.4 BILLION ANNUALLY The European Central Bank will discuss raising banks' minimum reserve requirements from 1% to 2% on November 25, Reuters reports. The move would require lenders to hold more non-interest-bearing reserves, saving euro-area central banks approximately €4.4 billion annually while withdrawing liquidity from the financial system. A majority of ECB governors, including the vice-president and chief economist, reportedly support the proposal. A decision could be delayed until December 17. The change would reduce central-bank losses but could pressure commercial bank profitability and lending capacity.

text: FED'S WALLER CALLS FOR 50-BASIS-POINT RATE HIKE IN DECEMBER Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller argues the Fed should consider a 50-basis-point rate hike in December rather than splitting tightening into 25-basis-point increases in December and January. Waller cited three consecutive 0.3% monthly core CPI readings, implying annualized inflation near 3.5%, well above the Fed's 2% target. He warned that delaying tightening could weaken the market signal. “My view is then you have to go 50 in December to put it in place and get it done.” His comments reinforce expectations of a more aggressive Fed tightening cycle.

text: $SPCX $APO - SPACEX PLANS $40 BILLION OFF-BALANCE-SHEET AI CHIP FINANCING SpaceX is preparing a $40 billion financing deal arranged by Apollo Global Management to fund AI chips without adding the debt directly to its balance sheet. The financing will use a special-purpose vehicle (SPV), allowing SpaceX to rent GPUs from its subsidiary. Apollo is expected to initially provide nearly $20 billion, before distributing the debt to investors. The structure highlights rising AI infrastructure financing costs and growing reliance on off-balance-sheet debt.

text: U.S. HOUSING STARTS SURGE 9.9%, BEATING FORECASTS, WHILE BUILDING PERMITS SLUMP U.S. housing starts jumped 9.9% in October to an annualized 1.309 million units, beating the 1.245 million consensus and reversing September's 7.0% decline. Single-family starts rose 4.0% to 864,000, while multifamily construction surged 23.6% to 445,000. However, building permits fell 7.4% to 1.295 million, missing expectations of 1.377 million. Single-family permits dropped 8.7%, suggesting the construction rebound may be difficult to sustain amid elevated borrowing costs.

text: HIGHER INTEREST RATES THREATEN CREDIT MARKETS AS PRIVATE LENDING DEMAND RISES Rising borrowing costs could push more companies away from public debt markets and toward private credit, according to executives at Bloomberg's Global Credit Forum. KKR warns that distressed debt ratios in U.S. and European leveraged loans and high-yield bonds could climb to 8%–9%, signaling mounting financial pressure. Meanwhile, HSBC identifies private credit as a major vulnerability, particularly loans issued to highly leveraged middle-market companies. text: UKRAINIAN DRONE STRIKES SLASH RUSSIAN OIL REFINING BY 45%, THREATENING FUEL SUPPLIES Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russia's crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, according to industry estimates cited by Reuters. Operations at 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries have been disrupted or halted, up from nine last week. Daily refining volumes have fallen from over 700,000 metric tons to roughly 400,000 tons, equivalent to approximately 3 million barrels per day. The escalating strikes threaten to worsen Russian fuel shortages, constrain exports and tighten global diesel markets.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: U.S. PENDING HOME SALES PLUNGE 4.7%, MORE THAN DOUBLE EXPECTATIONS U.S. pending home sales fell 4.7% in October, sharply missing expectations for a 2.0% decline, according to the National Association of Realtors. The index dropped to 63.0, down from 66.1 in September, while sales plunged 16.7% year over year. Weakness extended across all four regions, with the West and South recording the steepest monthly declines. The disappointing figures signal continued deterioration in U.S. housing demand, as elevated mortgage rates and affordability pressures weigh on prospective buyers.

text: SITUATIONAL AWARENESS PLANS COMEBACK AFTER $20 BILLION AI HEDGE FUND NEARLY COLLAPSED Leopold Aschenbrenner, the 25-year-old founder of Situational Awareness, is reportedly planning a comeback just four months after leveraged AI-stock bets nearly destroyed his hedge fund. Dubbed “Situational Awareness 2.0,” the plan could involve renewed leverage and fresh investor capital, according to the Financial Times. The fund previously managed over $20 billion before requiring an emergency rescue from Citadel. It still oversees more than $10 billion, including an approximately $5 billion stake in Anthropic. The proposed relaunch raises fresh questions about leverage, risk management and AI-sector concentration.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: FED'S BARR BACKS FURTHER RATE HIKES AS INFLATION REMAINS TOO HIGH Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr signaled support for additional interest-rate increases if the U.S. economy develops as expected. Barr warned that inflation remains too high, putting significant pressure on American households, and stressed the need to return inflation to the 2% target. He described the economy as strong, citing low unemployment, resilient consumer spending and robust business investment. Markets widely expect a 25-basis-point hike on December 9, bringing the federal funds target range to 4.00%–4.25%. His comments reinforce the Fed's increasingly hawkish policy outlook.

text: FED MINUTES SIGNAL FURTHER RATE HIKES, WITH 50-BASIS-POINT MOVE ON THE TABLE Nearly all Federal Reserve officials judged additional rate hikes likely appropriate, according to minutes of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. While most supported holding rates steady in October, some favored an immediate 25-basis-point increase. A couple of policymakers said a hike larger than 25 basis points in December could be warranted if inflation data deteriorated. Officials also warned that persistent inflation may require more restrictive monetary policy. The Fed discussed AI investment, productivity and financial stability, underscoring risks surrounding the economic outlook.

text: JPMORGAN SEES THREE MORE FED RATE HIKES AS U.S. GROWTH AND AI SPENDING MODERATE IN 2027 JPMorgan forecasts 1.9% U.S. GDP growth in 2027 on a fourth-quarter-over-fourth-quarter basis. The bank expects the AI investment cycle to mature, with real business capital expenditure growth slowing from 10% in 2026 to 8% in 2027. JPMorgan also predicts three Fed rate hikes in December, January and March, lifting the federal funds target range to 4.50%–4.75%. The bank says further tightening would aim to preserve the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, rather than deliberately weaken the labor market.

text: GLOBAL MARKETS BRACE FOR INTEREST RATES TO STAY ELEVATED THROUGH 2031 Traders increasingly expect the Federal Reserve, ECB and Bank of England to keep interest rates elevated for years after completing further hikes in 2027, according to Bloomberg. Interest-rate futures suggest little easing through at least 2031, marking a potential shift toward a structurally higher-rate environment. Persistent inflation, the Iran war, record AI-related borrowing, defense spending and infrastructure investment are keeping upward pressure on yields. JPMorgan expects another record year of U.S. investment-grade bond issuance in 2027. The outlook signals a prolonged era of higher financing costs for governments, businesses and households.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: FED'S JEFFERSON WARNS AI INVESTMENT BOOM IS FUELING INFLATION Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson says the massive AI infrastructure buildout is putting upward pressure on inflation by boosting demand across the economy. Jefferson described AI as both a demand and supply shock, with immediate inflationary pressures potentially offset by productivity gains in the future. He also warned that AI-driven job displacement could create significant challenges for households, even as new employment opportunities emerge. Jefferson highlighted the difficult trade-offs posed by energy price shocks but offered no guidance on future Fed rate decisions.

Cybersecurity firm SOCRadar identified the ransomware group n0n as claiming responsibility. Visa says no card numbers or payment data were compromised. Mastercard confirms limited customer information was exposed but says its payment network remains unaffected. JPMorgan says attackers may have accessed customer names, email addresses and marketing data. All three firms say core services remain operational, with JPMorgan confirming the breach is unrelated to its earlier banking outage.

text: GERMANY, FRANCE, UK AND UKRAINE DEMAND WINTER ENERGY CEASEFIRE FROM RUSSIA Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine issued a joint statement reaffirming their unwavering support for Kyiv. The leaders announced plans to increase missile-defense assistance ahead of winter and called on Russia to agree to an energy ceasefire throughout the winter as a first step toward ending hostilities. They also insisted that any future ceasefire must include robust, legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine. The coalition warned that Russia cannot outlast Western support or Ukraine's resilience, signaling a sustained commitment to Kyiv.

text: TRUMP SAYS XI AND PUTIN WANT IRAN WAR TO END, ARE PRESSURING TEHRAN President Donald Trump says China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin want the war with Iran to end and are communicating that position directly to Tehran. Trump said the conflict was discussed during his trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin, although Ukraine remained the primary focus. The remarks suggest potential diplomatic pressure from Beijing and Moscow to bring the conflict to an end.
